newsitem.title: USA: Army expects $996 million in yearly base savings.
newsitem.headline: Army expects $996 million in yearly base savings.

text.p: The Army said Monday that savings have overtaken costs in closing or realigning 803 of its bases around the world and it expects to save $996 million a year as a result.
It said savings overtook the $5.3 billion cost of closing the bases in mid-April.

The Army said it is in the ninth year of a 13-year programme to carry out required closing of 112 U.S. bases, realignment of 27 others which usually means reducing them, and closing or realigning 664 overseas bases.
The closings and realignments were ordered by four special base closing commissions with the approval of Congress and presidents Ronald Reagan, George Bush and Bill Clinton.
The Army said it was speeding up base closings and realignments where possible and in some cases the bases were successfully being converted to civilian use.

It said Detroit Diesel Corp., for example, is turning the Tooele Army maintenance depot in Utah into a remanufacturing hub; the University of California has a new campus at former Fort Ord and Cameron Station, Va., has been sold for a townhouse and condominium complex.
